title: Sequencing a day out
goal: Tell the story of a day out in order with d'abord, ensuite, puis, après ça and enfin, choosing avoir or être for each verb.

items.en: sequencing connectors in a past story

drills.text: ___, nous sommes allés au Parlement. Ensuite, on a mangé.
drills.en: First, we went to Parliament. Then we ate.

drills.text: On a visité le musée, ___ on a pris un café.
drills.en: We visited the museum, then we had a coffee.
drills.explain: [[puis]] = then; it often links two actions in the same sentence.

drills.prompt: “We waited for two hours, but in the end the show was cancelled.” Which word fits “in the end”?
drills.explain: [[finalement]] = in the end, eventually (often a result or a change of plan).

blocks.title: Raj's blog: “Our first Canada Day”
blocks.fr:
Le premier juillet, ma femme Priya et moi, nous sommes allés à Ottawa pour la fête du Canada.
D'abord, nous sommes partis de Montréal à sept heures et nous sommes arrivés à Ottawa vers neuf heures et demie. Il y a eu beaucoup de circulation !
Ensuite, nous sommes montés sur la colline du Parlement pour voir le spectacle. Il y a eu des chanteurs, des danseurs et des avions dans le ciel.
Vers midi, nous sommes descendus au Marché By et nous avons mangé une queue de castor, bien sûr. Puis, nous avons traversé le pont pour aller à Gatineau, au Musée canadien de l'histoire.
Après ça, nous nous sommes reposés au bord de la rivière. Plus tard, il a commencé à pleuvoir, mais finalement, la pluie s'est arrêtée à 21 h.
Enfin, à 22 h, nous avons regardé le feu d'artifice. Nous sommes rentrés à deux heures du matin, très fatigués mais très contents !
blocks.en: On July 1st, my wife Priya and I went to Ottawa for Canada Day. First, we left Montréal at seven and arrived in Ottawa around nine thirty. There was a lot of traffic! Next, we went up Parliament Hill to see the show. There were singers, dancers and planes in the sky. Around noon, we went down to the ByWard Market and ate a BeaverTail, of course. Then we crossed the bridge to go to Gatineau, to the Canadian Museum of History. After that, we rested by the river. Later, it started to rain, but in the end the rain stopped at 9 p.m. Finally, at 10 p.m., we watched the fireworks. We got home at two in the morning, very tired but very happy!

blocks.prompt: What did Raj and Priya do right after lunch?
options: They crossed the bridge to the museum in Gatineau.
blocks.explain: [[Puis, nous avons traversé le pont pour aller à Gatineau.]] Parliament Hill was before lunch; the fireworks were at the end.

blocks.prompt: What does “finalement, la pluie s'est arrêtée” mean here?
options: In the end, the rain stopped.
Finally, at last, the rain started.
blocks.explain: [[finalement]] = in the end. [[s'arrêter]] = to stop (reflexive → être, and [[pluie]] is feminine → [[arrêtée]]).

blocks.title: Sequencing words
head: Word
Meaning
Typical use
rows: a new step, often at the start of a sentence
links two actions, often in one sentence
a new step; après + noun: après le dîner
a result, often after a problem
blocks.note: Don't use the same word every time: [[d'abord… ensuite… puis… après ça… enfin]] makes your story sound organized and natural.

blocks.title: A story frame
blocks.pattern: D'abord, … Ensuite, … Puis … Après ça, … Enfin, …
blocks.note: Put the connector at the **start** of the sentence, usually followed by a comma. [[puis]] can also sit in the middle: [[On a mangé, puis on est partis.]]

examples.fr: D'abord, je suis allé à la banque.
examples.en: First, I went to the bank.

examples.fr: Ensuite, j'ai pris le métro jusqu'au centre-ville.
examples.en: Then I took the metro downtown.

examples.fr: J'ai acheté un cadeau, puis je suis rentré.
examples.en: I bought a present, then I went home.

examples.fr: Enfin, je me suis couché à minuit.
examples.en: Finally, I went to bed at midnight.

blocks.title: Avoir or être? A quick decision
blocks.body:
In a real story, you switch helper verbs all the time. Check each verb in this order:

1. **Is it reflexive** ([[se lever, se reposer, s'arrêter…]])? → **être**
2. **Is it in the house of être** ([[aller, venir, partir, arriver, monter, descendre, rester, rentrer, tomber, naître…]])? → **être**, and make it agree
3. **Everything else** → **avoir**, no agreement with the subject

And a useful past form: [[il y a eu]] = *there was / there were* (an event): [[Il y a eu un spectacle]], [[Il y a eu beaucoup de circulation]]. One more irregular participle: [[vouloir → voulu]], as in [[On a voulu sortir]] (we wanted to go out).

- **Enfin vs finalement:** [[enfin]] = the last step, or *at last!* ([[Enfin, tu es là !]]). [[finalement]] = *in the end*, after a change: [[On a voulu sortir, mais finalement, on est restés à la maison.]] English *finally* covers both.
- **Premièrement** (firstly) exists, but in a story about your day, [[d'abord]] is far more natural.
- **Après + verb:** [[Après manger]] is informal. At A2, say [[Après le dîner]] or [[Après ça]].
- **Alors is not a sequencing word:** in a story, [[alors]] usually means *so* (a consequence): [[Il a plu, alors on est rentrés.]] For the next step, use [[ensuite]] or [[puis]].

blocks.title: Ottawa and Gatineau
blocks.body:
Ottawa (Ontario) and Gatineau (Québec) face each other across the [[rivière des Outaouais]] (Ottawa River). Many people live in one city and work in the other, and you hear both French and English everywhere. On the Québec side, the region is called [[l'Outaouais]]; the whole area on both sides of the river is the National Capital Region ([[la région de la capitale nationale]]).

[[La fête du Canada]] is on July 1st. In Québec, [[la Fête nationale]] (Saint-Jean-Baptiste) is on June 24, and July 1st is also the traditional [[jour du déménagement]] (moving day), when many leases end!

blocks.prompt: Tell a friend about a recent day out (a festival, a trip to another city, a day downtown) in at least five steps, using five different connectors.
checklist: d'abord, ensuite, puis, après ça, enfin (or finalement)
At least one time: vers midi, à 15 h
A final feeling: très fatigué / fatiguée, mais content / contente

models.label: Model answer
models.fr: Samedi, je suis allée au Festival de jazz avec Lucie. D'abord, on s'est retrouvées au métro Place-des-Arts. Ensuite, on a écouté un concert gratuit. Vers 19 h, on a mangé une pizza, puis on est allées voir un deuxième spectacle. Après ça, on s'est promenées dans le Vieux-Montréal. Enfin, je suis rentrée à une heure du matin, très fatiguée mais contente !
models.en: (A woman speaking.) On Saturday I went to the Jazz Festival with Lucie. First, we met at Place-des-Arts metro. Next, we listened to a free concert. Around 7 p.m., we ate a pizza, then we went to see a second show. After that, we walked around Old Montréal. Finally, I got home at one in the morning, very tired but happy!

blocks.prompt: Write a short blog post like Raj's about a day out (real or imagined) in Ottawa, Gatineau, Québec City or your own city. Tell it in order.
checklist: Five connectors: d'abord, ensuite, puis, après ça, enfin
Approximate times: vers midi, vers 15 h
Avoir verbs, être verbs (with agreement) and one reflexive verb
How you felt at the end

models.label: Model answer
models.fr: Dimanche dernier, je suis allé à Gatineau avec mon colocataire. D'abord, nous avons visité le Musée canadien de l'histoire. Ensuite, nous avons fait du vélo dans le parc de la Gatineau. Vers 16 h, nous nous sommes arrêtés pour boire un café, puis nous avons pris des photos du lac. Nous avons voulu manger au restaurant, mais finalement, nous sommes rentrés à Ottawa. Enfin, nous avons mangé une pizza à la maison. Une très belle journée !
models.en: (A man writing.) Last Sunday I went to Gatineau with my roommate. First, we visited the Canadian Museum of History. Next, we went cycling in Gatineau Park. Around 4 p.m., we stopped for a coffee, then we took photos of the lake. We wanted to eat at a restaurant, but in the end we went back to Ottawa. Finally, we ate a pizza at home. A really nice day!

summary:
- Put events in order: [[d'abord, ensuite, puis, après ça, plus tard, enfin]]
- Say *in the end* with [[finalement]] and *around noon* with [[vers midi]]
- Choose **avoir** or **être** for each verb in one story, with agreement after être
- Use [[il y a eu]] for *there was / there were*

meta.notes: Corrected the Outaouais claim (it is the Québec-side region, not the whole area). Added missing accepts to r5 and r9, and tightened the alors and avoir/être explanations. “On a voulu” stays as a glossed form and is never tested.
